title: Injective abelian sections on a hypercover of an arbitrary site
statement:
Let $\mathcal D$ be a small site with finite limits [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention], let $W\in\mathcal D$, and let $V_\bullet$ be a simplicial object of $\mathcal D$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object] with an augmentation $V_\bullet\to W$ (a natural map to the constant simplicial object $W$). Set $N_0=W$; for $p>0$ let $N_p$ be the finite limit in $\mathcal D/W$ of the compatible proper faces of a $p$-simplex. Assume the sieve generated by $V_p\to N_p$ is covering for every $p\geq0$: there is a covering $\{N_{p,k}\to N_p\}_k$ of $\mathcal D$ each member of which factors through $V_p\to N_p$. Let $I$ be an injective abelian sheaf on $\mathcal D$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. With $d_i:V_{p+1}\to V_p$ the face maps, define $C^p(V,I)=I(V_p)$ for $p\geq0$, with differential $\delta^p=\sum_{i=0}^{p+1}(-1)^i d_i^*$. Then the restriction augmentation makes the sequence of abelian groups
$$0\longrightarrow I(W)\longrightarrow I(V_0)\xrightarrow{\delta^0} I(V_1)\xrightarrow{\delta^1}I(V_2)\longrightarrow\cdots$$
exact. In particular its degree-zero identification is induced by restriction from $W$. The topology need not be subcanonical, and the hypercover need not be split.

source.place: Tag 01GW, lemma-injective-trivial-cech; representable special case, with covering-sieve hypotheses as in Tag 01GE, lemma-acyclic-hypercover-sheaves. No subcanonicality hypothesis.

proof.text: Let $\mathbf Z[V_p]$ be the sheafified free abelian sheaf on the representable $V_p$. The free-resolution node gives an exact augmented alternating-face complex $\cdots\to\mathbf Z[V_2]\to\mathbf Z[V_1]\to\mathbf Z[V_0]\to\mathbf Z[W]\to0$. By the free representable Hom-to-sections bijection, applying $\operatorname{Hom}(-,I)$ identifies its dual cochain terms with $I(V_p)$ and the dual face maps with the alternating restriction differential $\delta^p$.

source.place: Tag 01GW proof, equation identifying the Cech complex with Hom from the sheafified free simplicial complex.

proof.text: Injectivity of $I$ makes $\operatorname{Hom}(-,I)$ exact on the displayed augmented complex. At positive degree, a cocycle $f:F_p\to I$ vanishes on $\operatorname{im}(d_{p+1})=\ker(d_p)$, so it factors through the monomorphism $\operatorname{im}(d_p)\hookrightarrow F_{p-1}$; extend that map to $F_{p-1}$ using the defining extension property of an injective object, and the resulting cochain has coboundary $f$. In degree zero, a cocycle $f:F_0\to I$ vanishes on $\operatorname{im}(d_1)=\ker(\varepsilon)$ for the augmentation $\varepsilon:F_0\to\mathbf Z[W]$, which is an epimorphism by exactness at $\mathbf Z[W]$; so $f$ factors uniquely through $\varepsilon$, which identifies the kernel of $\delta^0$ with the image of restriction from $I(W)$. Since $\varepsilon$ is an epimorphism, $\operatorname{Hom}(\varepsilon,I)$ is injective, which is exactness at $I(W)$.

source.place: Tag 01GW, proof after the Hom identification: injectivity and exactness of the free sheaf complex.

proof.text: Under the Hom-to-sections identifications, the map induced by $\mathbf Z[V_{p+1}]\to\mathbf Z[V_p]$ is $d_i^*:I(V_p)\to I(V_{p+1})$; summing with signs gives exactly $\delta^p$. The augmentation is restriction $I(W)\to I(V_0)$, so the preceding exactness is the stated sequence, including its degree-zero identification. No step uses subcanonicity or a splitting of the hypercover.

The item statement matches the live base exactly, so it was not weakened. It is the representable case of 01GW. With matching objects taken in D/W, p=1 gives V0 x_W V0 and p>=2 gives a connected limit equal to the coskeleton in 01GE. Yoneda preserves these limits, so a covering sieve is the same as being surjective after sheafification. The item assumes no subcanonicity and no splitness, and its proof uses neither. Step 1 is 01GW's Hom identification, using the new free-resolution node and the Mathlib leaf. Step 2 is the correct extension argument for an injective; in degree zero it only said 'same argument'. Step 3 is elementary: the free map on d_i sends the generator id to d_i, and naturality turns that into d_i^*. The new node lem-trf-site-hypercover-free-resolution is 01GE in the representable case. It is strictly smaller than the item and is not one of its clauses restated. I tested it on the identity hypercover (differentials alternate 0 and id, so it is exact) and on a Cech nerve (01GC). lean.statement: theorem siteHypercover_injective_sections_exact {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [HasFiniteLimits C] (J : Precoverage C) (hsite : J.IsSiteForCoverings) (W : C) (U : SimplicialObject C) (e : U ⟶ (Functor.const SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ).obj W) (hcover : ∀ (n : ℕ) (T : C) (w : T ⟶ W) (p : ∀ (Δ : SimplexCategory), Δ.len < n → (Δ ⟶ SimplexCategory.mk n) → (T ⟶ U.obj (op Δ))), (∀ (Δ : SimplexCategory) (h : Δ.len < n) (θ : Δ ⟶ SimplexCategory.mk n), p Δ h θ ≫ e.app (op Δ) = w) → (∀ (Δ Δ' : SimplexCategory) (h : Δ.len < n) (h' : Δ'.len < n) (α : Δ' ⟶ Δ) (θ : Δ ⟶ SimplexCategory.mk n), p Δ h θ ≫ U.map α.op = p Δ' h' (α ≫ θ)) → ∃ S : Sieve T, S ∈ J.toGrothendieck T ∧ ∀ (V : C) (f : V ⟶ T), S f → ∃ t : V ⟶ U _⦋n⦌, t ≫ e.app (op (SimplexCategory.mk n)) = f ≫ w ∧ ∀ (Δ : SimplexCategory) (h : Δ.len < n) (θ : Δ ⟶ SimplexCategory.mk n), t ≫ U.map θ.op = f ≫ p Δ h θ) (I : Sheaf J.toGrothendieck AddCommGrpCat.{max u v r}) [Injective I] : Function.Injective (I.obj.map (e.app (op (SimplexCategory.mk 0))).op) ∧ Function.Exact (I.obj.map (e.app (op (SimplexCategory.mk 0))).op) (fun s : I.obj.obj (op (U _⦋0⦌)) ↦ ∑ j : Fin 2, (-1 : ℤ) ^ j.val • I.obj.map (U.δ j).op s) ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, Function.Exact (fun s : I.obj.obj (op (U _⦋n⦌)) ↦ ∑ j : Fin (n + 2), (-1 : ℤ) ^ j.val • I.obj.map (U.δ j).op s) (fun s : I.obj.obj (op (U _⦋n + 1⦌)) ↦ ∑ j : Fin (n + 3), (-1 : ℤ) ^ j.val • I.obj.map (U.δ j).op s)
